speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
before: Gate stays open. Always has. My girl's still up that road somewhere, and I'd hate for her to come home and find it shut.
after: Gate stays open. Always has. My girl's still up that road somewhere, and I'd hate for her to come home one night and find it shut.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
before: Four Paths kept that city alive. Beefcakes ran the lights, Gourmands the kitchens, Necrocrats the graveyards, Refusemancers the bins. Then {villain} chained all four.
after: Four Paths kept that city alive. Beefcakes ran the lights, Gourmands the kitchens, Necrocrats the graveyards, Refusemancers the bins. Then {villain} put all four in chains.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
before: My girl Isla went up that road eight years ago. If you see her... tell her the gate is still open.
after: My girl Isla went up that road eight years ago. If you see her up there... tell her the gate is still open.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
before: Hm. Each zone you free turns another service back on, and the castle gets a little less frightening. My knees, sadly, are a local problem.
after: Hm. Each zone you free turns a service back on, and the castle gets a little less frightening. Can't say the same for my knees.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Evening! Old Hob, at your service. I dig, mostly, though there's not been much call for it these ten years. Nobody's been collected, you see. Paperwork. Heh.
after: Evening! Old Hob, at your service. I dig, mostly, though there's not been a lot of call for it these ten years. Nobody's been collected, you see. Paperwork. Heh.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Appointments. Let's have a look for you... hm. Not for a good long while yet. Lovely! That's what I like to see.
after: Appointments. Let's have a look for you, shall we... hm. Not for a good long while yet. Lovely! That's what I like to see.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Mind the cairn at the end of the row. Something under it is still counting its turns, and it's rude to keep a thing like that waiting. Heh.
after: Mind the cairn at the end of the row, though. Something under it is still counting its turns, and it's rude to keep a thing like that waiting. Heh.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Still digging, slowly. Two particular graves, these ten years now. I like to take my time over the important ones. Heh.
after: Still digging, and taking it slowly. Two particular graves I've been at, these ten years now. I like to take my time over the important ones. Heh.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Appointments. Let's have a look for you... hm. Not for a good long while yet. Lovely! That's what I like to see.
after: Appointments. Let's have a look for you, shall we... hm. Not for a good long while yet. Lovely! That's what I like to see.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: I'd charge a handling fee, but you've nothing I want. Heh.
after: I'd charge you a handling fee for the trouble, only you've nothing on you that I want. Heh.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: The intake's open again, did you hear? Busy week. Gerald's number finally came up, lovely chap. He asked if he could stay on for one more pot first, and I said yes. No rush, in my line.
after: The intake's open again, did you hear? Busy week. Gerald's number finally came up, lovely chap, and he asked if he could stay on for one more pot first. I said yes. There's no rush, in my line.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Agnes stayed on, of course. Somebody has to fix the forms, and I've pencilled her in for later. Much later. Heh.
after: Agnes stayed on, of course. Somebody has to put the forms right, so I've pencilled her in for later. Much later. Heh.

speaker: (narration)
before: A narrow gap in the old treeline - easy to miss, easy enough to slip through, if you're not afraid of a shortcut.
after: There is a narrow gap in the old treeline here. It would be easy to miss, and easy enough to slip through, if you aren't afraid of a shortcut.
